Six seconds. 

Six seconds is an ungodly amount of time behind the line of scrimmage for a quarterback. Joe Burrow had six seconds behind the line of scrimmage last night before hitting Chase Brown on a 4-yard touchdown. Then, Joe Burrow had six seconds behind the line of scrimmage before he hit Drew Sample on a 3-yard touchdown. Joe Burrow is completely in his bag right now, and playing the quarterback position as well as he has his entire career. Last night's performance against the Steelers was another masterpiece, a five game stretch in which he's had 4 touchdowns in each, the first player to do that since Peyton Manning's record breaking 2004 season. He also completed 13 of 13 passes against the blitz. BUt those six seconds are huge. Those six seconds, and the protection he's getting, might be the difference from this high flying Joe Burrow season and the ones before it. 

Shoutout to Amarius Mims, Dalton Risner, Ted Karras, Dylan Fairchild, and Orlando Brown, Jr. 

The offensive line deserves a ton of love. Six seconds are an eternity.
